title: 12 Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Melbourne (2026)
description: The 12 best specialty coffee shops in Melbourne, curated from Reddit. Find the best flat whites, pour-overs, and espresso in the CBD, Collingwood, Fitzroy, and more. Interactive map included.

places.name: Patricia Coffee Brewers

redditQuotes.text: Patricia is THE Melbourne coffee experience — standing room only, no wifi, just perfect coffee.
The flat white at Patricia is the benchmark against which all others are measured.

places.verdict: Best for: The most quintessential Melbourne coffee experience — standing in a laneway with a perfect flat white.

places.name: Proud Mary Coffee

redditQuotes.text: Proud Mary ranked #4 in the world for a reason — their espresso flights are a masterclass.
If you visit one roastery in Melbourne, make it Proud Mary in Collingwood.

places.verdict: Best for: Single-origin pour-overs and espresso flights from a globally ranked roastery.

places.name: Seven Seeds Coffee Roasters

redditQuotes.text: Seven Seeds is where Melbourne's modern coffee culture started. Still one of the best.
The warehouse space in Carlton is beautiful — great for a slow morning coffee.

places.verdict: Best for: The roastery that defined Melbourne's third-wave movement — clean, balanced, sustainable.

places.name: Brother Baba Budan

redditQuotes.text: Brother Baba Budan is where Melbourne coffee culture was born — and the hanging chairs are iconic.
Go early before the tourists arrive. The coffee is genuinely excellent, not just a gimmick.

places.verdict: Best for: The most Instagram-famous café in Melbourne — chairs bolted to the ceiling and Seven Seeds coffee.

places.name: ST. ALi Coffee Roasters

redditQuotes.text: St Ali was doing specialty coffee before specialty coffee was cool. Still pushing boundaries.
The brunch menu is as good as the coffee — and that's saying something in Melbourne.

places.verdict: Best for: Brunching alongside world-class espresso in a trendy warehouse space.

places.name: Market Lane Coffee

redditQuotes.text: Market Lane at Queen Vic Market is perfect for a Saturday morning filter after browsing the stalls.
Their seasonal single-origins are always interesting — you can taste the transparency.

places.verdict: Best for: Seasonal pour-overs with total transparency on sourcing — the thinking drinker's roastery.

places.name: Industry Beans

redditQuotes.text: Industry Beans Fitzroy is worth visiting for the space alone — but the coffee and food are equally impressive.
Their deconstructed lattes and creative drinks push the boundary of what a café can be.

places.verdict: Best for: The best brunch-meets-coffee experience in Melbourne — innovative food paired with excellent espresso.

places.name: Code Black Coffee Roasters

redditQuotes.text: Code Black in Brunswick is quintessential Melbourne coffee — industrial space, serious roasting, killer long black.
If you like your coffee with more body and depth, Code Black is your spot.

places.verdict: Best for: Rich, full-bodied espresso from a competition-grade roaster in an industrial-chic setting.

places.name: Axil Coffee Roasters

redditQuotes.text: Axil's baristas have won Australian championships — you can taste the precision in every cup.
The Magic coffee at Axil is a Melbourne invention you need to try.

places.verdict: Best for: Competition-winning baristas serve technically perfect espresso — the barista's barista choice.

places.name: Dukes Coffee Roasters

redditQuotes.text: Dukes on Flinders Lane is where I send every visitor who asks for the best coffee in the CBD.
Clean, consistent, and the wood-panelled interior is gorgeous.

places.verdict: Best for: A refined CBD espresso bar tucked into Flinders Lane — beautiful design, flawless execution.

places.name: Aunty Peg's

redditQuotes.text: Aunty Peg's is where the serious coffee nerds go — lever espresso, rare micro-lots, incredible space.
If you're a professional roaster visiting Melbourne, Aunty Peg's is mandatory.

places.verdict: Best for: The coffee nerd's pilgrimage — rare lots, experimental processing, and lever espresso machines.

places.name: Padre Coffee

redditQuotes.text: Padre has trained half the baristas in Melbourne — their beans are consistently excellent for home brewing.
The Lygon St roastery is a quiet gem away from the tourist spots.

places.verdict: Best for: Taking home Melbourne's best beans — plus on-site education for aspiring home baristas.
